source_observations: Upstream explicitly lists German among the 11 recommended languages for Audio8 TTS Preview 0.6B. This grants German source eligibility only; no Frankenstein German listening or runtime quality credit is implied.

The main model is reported as 601,159,424 parameters excluding the codec and uses a DualAR design: a slow autoregressive semantic-token transformer followed by a fast autoregressive codec-codebook predictor.

The bundled codec is 44.1 kHz with 2,048 samples per model frame, approximately 21.5 model frames per second. The checkpoint supports zero-shot voice cloning from reference audio plus an exact reference transcript.

The ordinary Hugging Face Transformers path contains custom Python model/processor/codec code and upstream explicitly instructs callers to review it and use trust_remote_code=True. That path must not be treated as pre-audited target runtime code.

A separate first-party ONNX Runtime deployment exists for the same 0.6B family. It uses weight-only INT4 Slow/Fast AR graphs, FP16 activations/KV/cache and FP16 codec, and after model download does not require PyTorch, Transformers or Hugging Face Hub at runtime.

The first-party ONNX service exposes streaming signed-16-bit 44.1 kHz PCM and a cancellation endpoint, plus an OpenAI-compatible /v1/audio/speech WAV route. These interfaces are source-level alignment signals for the Frankenstein voice ABI, not measured barge-in or TTFA evidence.

The ONNX runtime serializes synthesis and voice-registration requests to bound memory. Upstream reports about 1004 MiB loaded and roughly 1.1-1.2 GiB synthesis peak on a tested 16 GB Apple M2, with about 572 MiB online model files and about 968 MiB including the optional registration encoder. Those numbers are upstream Apple-M2 measurements and cannot be transferred to clay-direct-dev without measurement.

The current ONNX release is explicitly tested on macOS arm64 CPUExecutionProvider. Linux CPU compatibility is plausible from the dependency/runtime design but was not observed in this source audit and receives zero target-runtime credit.

The pinned ONNX Python dependency set is small and explicit: numpy 2.4.3, onnxruntime 1.24.4, soundfile 0.13.1, scipy 1.17.1, fastapi 0.135.2, uvicorn 0.42.0, pydantic >=2.9,<3, python-multipart 0.0.22.

The ONNX artifact repository is Apache-2.0 and contains ONNX/Xet model data plus tokenizer/manifest files rather than Hugging Face custom Python model code. Model graphs remain untrusted executable inputs and still require isolated verification before target adoption.

Upstream recommends keeping synthesis inputs within 150 characters for best quality. Frankenstein therefore needs its own incremental text segmentation and prosody-continuity test rather than assuming long-response quality from single-shot samples.

torch_transformers_path.target_recommendation: Do not use directly in F2 target runtime before code review and exact revision pinning.

onnx_cpu_path.remaining_risk: Untrusted ONNX graphs and Python service/runtime code still require isolated source/hash-bound verification; setup scripts and dependencies must be inspected/pinned before execution.

advantages_to_measure: German is an upstream-declared primary language
first-party zero-shot voice cloning could preserve a stable male acoustic identity
first-party CPU INT4 ONNX path could avoid GPU residency competition with the local dialogue LLM
streaming PCM plus explicit cancel route maps naturally to cancellable F2 playback
OpenAI-compatible speech route may reduce adapter complexity while preserving the existing voice-provider boundary
unproven_or_risks: German naturalness, pronunciation and prosody on the actual user/domain corpus
stable male voice identity across long sessions and segmented streaming
true time-to-first-audio and RTF on clay-direct-dev
Linux CPU provider behavior and thread contention with ASR/LLM/audio services
whether chunk boundaries create audible seams or prosody reset
whether cancel stops generation quickly enough for Frankenstein barge-in rather than only stopping HTTP delivery
voice cloning consent/provenance and exact reference-audio custody must remain explicit
the Transformers remote-code path should not be used merely because it is the default model-card example

hypothesis: Audio8 0.6B INT4 ONNX can become a high-value German local TTS challenger because it combines explicit German support, zero-shot voice identity, streaming/cancel interfaces and a low-memory CPU-only path that may preserve GPU budget for the dialogue brain.
counterhypothesis: Its autoregressive 44.1 kHz codec path may be too slow on the actual target CPU, segmented text may collapse prosody, and voice-cloning quality may not match the required stable male Frankenstein identity; Qwen3-TTS, MagpieTTS or a simpler Piper-class baseline may dominate the end-to-end latency/naturalness frontier.
